question.text: A steel tape measures the length of a copper rod as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>90</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> when both are at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, the calibration temperature for the tape. What would be the tape reading for the length of the rod when both are at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. Given, <math><mi>α</mi><mi> </mi></math>for steel<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi> </mi><mn>1.2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi> </mi></math>and<math><mi> </mi><mi>α</mi><mi> </mi></math>for copper is<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi> </mi><mn>1.7</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
As the steel tape is calibrated at 10 °C, therefore, adjacent centimeter marks on the steel tape will be separated by a distance of

lt=l101+ αs∆T=(1+αs20) cm

= 901+αc20cm

Therefore, number of centimeters read on the tape will be

= 901+αc2011+αs20= 901+1.7×10-5×2011+1.2×10-5×20

= 90×1.000341.00024=90.01 cm
